item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 220511
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Oct 21 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located several hundred miles south of Acapulco,
Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, a few hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll
late this weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter while the
system moves generally eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Storm Vance are issued under WMO
header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/advisories on Tropical Storm Vance are issued under WMO
header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...VANCE STRENGTHENING AS IT MOVES WESTWARD... As of 3:00 AM CST Thu Oct 22 the center of Vance was located near 9.7, -101.5 with movement W at 7 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1000 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 50 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 220847
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 AM CST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
...VANCE STRENGTHENING AS IT MOVES WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...9.7N 101.5W
ABOUT 510 MI...820 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 670 MI...1075 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 9.7 North, longitude 101.5 West. Vance is
moving toward the west near 7 mph (11 km/h). A turn to the
northwest is expected to occur over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Rapid intensification is expected during the next couple of days, 
and the system is forecast to become a major hurricane by Saturday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Wed Oct 21 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 220258
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
900 PM CST Wed Oct 21 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Vance continues to become better 
organized, with an expanding area of deep convection over the 
circulation and cloud-top temperatures as cold as -80 degrees 
C. The latest subjective intensity estimate from TAFB is 
T2.5/35 kt, while objective estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 32 to 
43 kt. Based on these estimates and the improving satellite 
presentation, the initial intensity has been increased to 40 kt.
 
The initial motion is estimated at 290/4 kt. The storm will begin to 
slow down as it turns northwest and then north-northwest, steered 
along the southern and western periphery of a mid-level ridge 
located over Mexico. The latest NHC track forecast is very similar 
to the previous advisory, with a slight eastward adjustment at days 
4 and 5 toward the latest GDMI, HCCA, and TVCN consensus aids. 
However, considerable cross-track spread remains among the guidance 
solutions at longer forecast ranges, likely related to differences 
in how the models depict the evolving synoptic pattern near the 
western United States. Consequently, confidence in the extended 
portion of the track forecast remains lower than normal.
 
Environmental conditions appear very favorable for significant 
strengthening during the next couple of days, with warm sea surface 
temperatures, low vertical wind shear, and plenty of deep-layer 
moisture.  SHIPS RII, DTOPS, and SDCON guidance continue to be 
supportive, suggesting over a 50 percent probability of extreme RI 
over the next 3 days, indicating a high-confidence scenario for a 
major hurricane to develop. Given the favorable environment and 
elevated rapid intensification probabilities, the updated NHC 
intensity forecast explicitly calls for rapid intensification during 
the next 2 to 3 days. By day 4, Vance will begin to experience 
increased vertical wind shear while moving into slightly drier 
mid-level air, suggesting a weakening trend thereafter.
